text: We will continue to develop Plaid Cymru’s Inspire Wales programme to involve all ages in sporting activity and ensure our people stay fit and healthy.
explanation: This is the exact negative example from the codebook: a straightforward programme commitment (sports participation for fitness and health) with purely instrumental language and no moral vocabulary.

text: Values of respect.
explanation: Explicit moral vocabulary: 'respect' is listed in the codebook's definition and clarification (a) as a core moral concept. Even though fragmentary, the text invokes a moral value directly.

text: • Waiting lists are not tolerable.
explanation: 'Not tolerable' is an explicit moral evaluation — the codebook lists 'tolerable/intolerable' as explicit moral vocabulary (clarification a) that frames an issue as a moral wrong rather than a neutral administrative target.

text: to ensure an efficient and accessible school bus system for communities across the country.
explanation: A neutral description of a policy goal (efficient and accessible school buses) using administrative/instrumental language; no moral-evaluative terms. Accessibility here is practical service provision, not a moral claim.

text: work with stakeholders to ensure ticket prices at sporting events do not unfairly discriminate against people from low socio economic backgrounds.
explanation: Contains explicit moral vocabulary: 'unfairly discriminate' combines the moral terms 'unfair' and 'discriminate', both listed in clarification (a) (fair/unfair, discriminated). The text frames pricing as a potential moral wrong against low-income people.

text: Much of the UK’s language, culture and way of life has been enriched by successive new arrivals over thousands of years.
explanation: A descriptive, factual-historical claim about cultural enrichment from immigration. 'Enriched' is a generic positive term, not moral vocabulary; there is no appeal to justice, rights, dignity, or moral duty.

text: The international evidence is clear:
explanation: A neutral empirical framing device introducing evidence; no moral vocabulary or evaluation of any kind.

text: and free prescriptions and eye tests for the over-60s, without means testing.
explanation: A description of a policy instrument (free prescriptions and eye tests without means testing) with no moral-evaluative language; purely programmatic.

text: In government, The Nationals will place any money left in this program in the hands of school boards and principals who are best placed to know how and where the priorities for their schools lie.
explanation: Technocratic administrative statement about devolving funding decisions to school boards and principals; no moral vocabulary, just an efficiency/local-knowledge rationale.

text: Revive the National Adult Learning Council and local co-ordinating bodies so that diverse elements of lifelong learning can be linked into one coherent system through which learners can progress.
explanation: Administrative programme description (reviving a council to coordinate lifelong learning); instrumental language with no moral evaluation.

text: And as I’ve mentioned, as a result of our initiative, the Three Strikes legislation was passed.
explanation: A factual claim about the passage of legislation; no moral-evaluative vocabulary or normative framing.

text: and stop unions looking to restrict their freedom to choose how they want to work.
explanation: Appeals to 'freedom to choose how they want to work' as a value being protected from unjust restriction. The codebook explicitly includes appeals to freedom/liberty as a value being protected or unjustly restricted.

text: Every person, however frail or vulnerable, has a place and a purpose in this world.
explanation: This is a positive example from the codebook: it affirms the inherent worth of every human being, 'however frail or vulnerable' — a direct moral claim about human dignity.

text: Ensure that all children will be tested in literacy and numeracy at two stages during their primary school education.
explanation: A neutral policy commitment on testing in schools; instrumental educational administration with no moral vocabulary.

text: - We have one court system
explanation: A bare factual/descriptive statement about institutional structure (one court system) with no moral-evaluative language.

text: Many new small businesses are started by women.
explanation: A factual/empirical claim about who starts small businesses; no moral vocabulary or normative judgment.

text: Our economy will be thriving, delivering balanced growth with jobs that last in every nation and region.
explanation: An aspirational economic vision using generic positive adjectives ('thriving', 'balanced growth') which the negative clarification explicitly excludes; jobs and growth framing is economic, not moral.

text: courts and tribunals that are independent of the government of the day.
explanation: A neutral description of institutional design (independent courts and tribunals). While judicial independence has normative significance, the text itself uses no moral-evaluative vocabulary and reads as a structural description.

text: While no one should be denied access to the courts, the rule of lawyers threatens our global competitiveness, denies Americans access to the quality of justice they deserve, and puts every small business one lawsuit away from bankruptcy.
explanation: This is a positive example from the codebook: it invokes justice and moral desert ('the quality of justice they deserve') and the ethical principle that no one should be denied access to the courts.

text: Prioritise the development of high-standard affordable homes by amending and expanding the use of Special Development Zones and / or a new permit scheme.

text: and contribute new technology.
explanation: Neutral fragment about contributing technology; no moral-evaluative content.

text: / and fast, frequent inner-city services.
explanation: Neutral description of transport services; no moral vocabulary.

explanation: Technocratic policy on permit processing for oil and gas exploration; instrumental language only.

text: Reduce by 50 per cent the rates bills of village shops, pubs and/or garages where they are the last one, two or three remaining in their communities.

text: · further support for back country reafforestation.
